title: Plural owner forms: meidän, teidän, heidän
summary: Use meidän, teidän, heidän before a supplied possessed noun.
objectives: Use meidän, teidän, heidän before a supplied possessed noun.
Apply this rule with the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: This pack groups several owners, not the number of owned things. meidän means “our”, teidän means “your” (a group), and heidän means “their”.

An owner form says whose thing something is. Put it before the possessed noun. The noun forms and Tämä on (“This is”) in these examples are supplied; you will learn the endings and sentence construction separately.
me (“we”) becomes meidän (“our”); te (“you”) becomes teidän (“your”); he (“they”) becomes heidän (“their”).
This owner group can own one thing or several things. The later lessons teach both object numbers.
keyPoints: Use meidän, teidän, heidän before a supplied possessed noun.

steps: Tämä on (“This is”) and the complete noun form are supplied.
Use meidän (“our”) before the noun; its basic personal form is me.
Tämä on (“This is”) and the complete noun form are supplied.
Use teidän (“your”) before the noun; its basic personal form is te.
Tämä on (“This is”) and the complete noun form are supplied.
Use heidän (“their”) before the noun; its basic personal form is he.

commonMistakes: Do not use me, te, he where an owner form is needed.
Use the supplied noun form; suffix formation is taught separately.
